statement: Ana, Ben and Cal stand on a number line. Ana is 3 to the left of Ben. Cal is 5 to the right of Ben. Cal stands at 17. Where does Ana stand?

choices.misconception: I found where Ben stands and stopped there.
I went 3 to the left of Cal instead of 3 to the left of Ben.
I found Ben at 12 and then went 3 to the right instead of the left.
I went to the right both times, 17 + 5 + 3.

hints: Whose place on the number line do you already know?
Draw a number line and mark Cal. Work backwards: Cal is to the right of Ben, so Ben is to the left of Cal. Then find Ana from Ben, not from Cal.
Ben is 5 to the left of Cal, so Ben is at 12. Ana is 3 to the left of Ben. Count 3 steps left from 12.

solutions.reliable: Cal is 5 to the right of Ben, so Ben is 5 to the left of Cal: $17 - 5 = 12$. Ana is 3 to the left of Ben: $12 - 3 = 9$. Check: from 9, 3 steps right is 12, where Ben is, and 5 more steps right is 17, where Cal is. The idea to keep: draw the number line, find who each clue is measured from, and move the right way.
solutions.elegant: Ben stands between Ana and Cal, so Ana is $3 + 5 = 8$ to the left of Cal: $17 - 8 = 9$. The idea to keep: when one point is between two others, the two gaps add up to the whole gap.

whyOnTest: Clues measured from different people and in both directions test whether a student can keep a number line straight.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
